Walking into Chin Chin Chu is like stepping into a high-fashion graphic novel. The design language is a playful nod to Chinoiserie, but through a filter of modern pop art.

featured_reviews.name: Vedant lad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dropped by this gem the other day we were at Juhu beach and this one is cited at a walk of 5 mins from the Novotel end. Talking about the ambience first, they have indoor as well as outdoor dining area. The entire space looks extremely vibrant and full of colours which looks absolutely beautiful. Coming to the f&b, for our first round of drinks we ordered for Kung Fu Panda which was a gin-based cocktail having refreshing elements like Basil, lemongrass ginger, star anise and passionfruit. Loved the way it was presented which made it totally gramworthy. Next, we had Golden dynasty from their Chinese new years menu, this one was vodka base and had lovely taste as it had citrusy elements. The food menu here is wide spread and offers almost everything you could think of. We tried their Philadelphia Cream cheese and miso Dimsums and hands down these are one of the finest cheese dimsums we have tried in a while. Next we had Crab Salad and tempura prawn sushi which also had cream cheese drizzled on top of it. Mild and mellow flavour profile yet the chef managed to make it so delectable. This one was so good that we had to repeat it. Upon or servers recommendation, we tried Prawns in butter garlic which was wok tossed prawns drenched in butter garlic sauce. Simple and perfect which can't go wrong. Later for the mains, we tried Exotic Mushroom clay pot rice which was topped with truffle butter sauce. The pot rice had a generous amount of veggies and especially mushrooms. We lastly ordered for Chilli garlic noodles which were thin noodles wok tossed in chilli garlic sauce along with chicken - this was totally worth every penny. Now for round two of drinks we tried chin chin gin and Oogway’s paloma which was again gin base cocktail. Both the cocktails were a solid 10.
For dessert, we had Nutella wellcake which was soft and gooey cake drenched in Nutella. Overall it was a lovely dining experience and we will be coming here again for sure.

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Sagar Chinese located at N S Rd No. 10, opposite Sukhmani Society, JVPD Scheme, Juhu — and honestly, it was such a satisfying experience! This spot is known to be a favourite of Kartik Aaryan, and after trying the food, we can totally understand why.

It’s a small, simple restaurant, but don’t judge it by its size — the Chinese cuisine here is absolutely amazing and full of flavour. Perfect for late-night cravings in Juhu!

Here’s what we tried:

• Chicken Lollypop Masala – Properly masaledar, nostalgic vibes, and super tasty. One of our favourites!
• Crispy Chicken – Perfectly crunchy on the outside, juicy inside. Fresh and delicious.
• Hunan Chicken (Dry) – Bold flavours, slightly spicy, and extremely satisfying. A must-try!
• Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice – Total game changer! Fully loaded, spicy, saucy, and easily the star of the meal.

The service and management were smooth and quick despite the rush. Staff was polite and the food arrived on time.

Overall, if you’re in Juhu and craving authentic, street-style Chinese — especially late at night — this place definitely deserves to be on your list. Affordable, tasty, and totally worth it! 🍜🔥

Together, they’ve earned quite a name for serving some of the best Indo-Chinese food in the Juhu–Andheri belt.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of desi Chinese, this little roadside gem in Juhu deserves a spot on your list. It’s operated by the same folks behind Sagar Chinese on the main Juhu Road — a name that’s already earned quite a loyal following among local foodies. Together, they’ve carved a niche for themselves as one of the best spots for authentic Indo-Chinese flavours in the Juhu–Andheri area.

The food here is everything you’d expect from a classic desi Chinese joint — bold, flavourful, and loaded with that unmistakable wok-tossed aroma. The portions are hearty, the pricing is fair, and the taste delivers every single time. Their Manchow Soup, Chicken Crispy, and Triple Rice are absolute standouts — dishes that perfectly balance spice, crunch, and comfort in true street-style fashion.

On the flip side, the service is quite disappointing — slow and uncoordinated, which tends to dull the otherwise satisfying experience. Seating is also limited, so it’s best to plan your visit accordingly.

Overall, despite the service hiccup, this place continues to shine for what matters most — good food that hits the spot without burning a hole in your pocket.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sampan delivers an authentic Asian dining experience with a well-curated menu and a vibrant ambiance. The décor, lighting, and setup reflect the essence of an upscale Asian restaurant, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere.

Food Highlights
1. Kung Pao Potato – Crispy potato cubes tossed in a flavorful, spicy-sweet sauce with crunchy peanuts and dried chilies, offering a satisfying bite.

2. Salt and Pepper Fish – Lightly battered fish fillets, stir-fried with salt, crushed pepper, and subtle spices, delivering a crispy yet tender texture.

3. Crunchy Lotus Stem – Thinly sliced lotus stems fried to perfection, coated in a tangy and slightly sweet glaze, making for an addictive appetizer.

4. Shanghai Chicken – Succulent chicken pieces cooked in a rich, umami-packed Shanghai-style sauce with a balanced hint of spice.

5. Crunchy Garlic Prawns – Medium sized prawns fried to a golden crisp and infused with a bold garlic flavor, enhancing their natural sweetness.

6. Fish and Prawns Fried Rice – Fragrant, well-seasoned fried rice generously loaded with mushrooms, fish and prawns, offering a hearty and flavorful main course.

7. Caramel Custard – A silky-smooth custard with a perfectly caramelized top, delivering a rich and creamy finish. Caramel was a bit bitter though.

8. Ice Cream with Litchi – A refreshing dessert where the creaminess of the ice cream complements the juicy sweetness of litchis. Canned litchies were served. Fresh litchies would taste even better.

Ambiance: Authentic Asian-themed with a cozy yet upscale feel.

Service: Professional and attentive staff, providing prompt service and answering queries efficiently.

Food Quantity: Portions were adequate and well-balanced.

Cleanliness & Hygiene: Well-maintained and hygienic dining space.

Impressed with its flavorful dishes, well-managed service, and immersive ambiance.
Definitely a must-visit for Asian cuisine lovers!

featured_reviews.review_text:
During my recent visit to Haochi Restaurant, I discovered a hidden gem within – Kabab Hut. This small yet vibrant spot left a lasting impression with its exceptional food and warm service.

The variety of kababs was a treat for the senses, with flavors that showcased skillful preparation. Among the selections, the Galouti Kababs stood out. They were incredibly fresh, succulent, and melted in the mouth – truly a must-try for kabab enthusiasts. Another dish we love was roti pe boti which had incredibly flavourful and soft meat served on a crunchy roti. Would definitely gonna have it again in my next visit.

LIIT was made perfectly with an adequate amount of alcohol to give you high in a single drink.

For starters, the Bok Choy Dimsum was another highlight. The dimsum was delicately crafted, juicy on the inside, and perfectly steamed, adding an authentic Asian flavour to our meal.

Moving to the main course, the Nalli Nihari was a masterpiece. The rich, aromatic gravy paired beautifully with the tender meat, which was cooked to perfection. The Roomali Roti accompanying it was soft and fresh, making the combination irresistible.

Special mention to our waiter, Mr. Laukik, who ensured we were comfortable and guided us through the menu with patience and expertise. His friendly demeanor added to the experience.

While there was a noticeable delay in serving the dishes, the quality of the food more than made up for it. A little improvement in timing could elevate the overall experience.

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Haaochi

Located in Sun-N- Sand, one of the famous and first beachside hotels of India. This place doesn’t need any introduction. I am glad to announce that this place is absolutely worth it. In the past few years, Haaochi has managed to get a hype for its Asian food, authenticity & their fine dine experience and no kidding, it was all worth the hype.

Ambience: The interiors are so good here. Well set tables with a comfortable seating area and positive vibes were welcoming us for the meal. The open kitchen is done in a classy way that is right in the middle of the restaurant. Lighting was perfect and beautifully done.

Food: I tried a bunch of things here.

Kimchi Salad: Spicy and cold kimchi salad was great, fulfilling and hearty.

I had assorted Veg and Non Veg dumplings which were steamed to perfection and filling. Also, they look damn amazing.

Chilli Mint Style Fish: A super amazing dish. The combo is so good. It will take your tastebuds to the next level. Must try!!!

Chow Chu Style Potatoes: As you can guess from the name this dish is their signature dish. I think they’ve never gone wrong with this. Made it to perfection.

Chow Chu Style Chicken: Chicken, Mushrooms and Cashew cooked in spicy sauce and presented beautifully. The chicken was soft, good and easy to bite.

Lotus Stem Root: Super palatable and crunchy. Can never go wrong.

Butter Garlic Rice: It was exceptionally good and worth having.

Veg Thai Curry: It was simply delectable and spicy. Loved to have this with butter garlic rice.

Chicken Pot Rice: You’ll love the savory flavor of the rice and it was a complete meal as it was loaded with veggies and chicken.

Yogurt Almond and Choco Lava Cake are desserts from which I love Choco Lava Cake more and it was so rich. Nothing can’t be better than these desserts. Do try.

Overall, they have well played with the menu. I would love to come again here to try some new delicacies here.

P.S: The review is strictly depending on my personal experience.

Food: 5/5

Ambience: 5/5

Value for Money: 5/5

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Vibrant Spot with a Kick: Blabber Juhu

​If you’re looking for a spot in Juhu that nails the "Instagrammable" aesthetic without sacrificing the quality of the meal, Blabber All Day is definitely worth a visit. Here is a breakdown of the experience:

​The Ambience
​The decor is easily the highlight. It’s elegant, whimsical, and filled with soft pastel hues and floral accents. Whether you’re looking for a brunch spot with friends or a cozy corner for a date, the atmosphere feels upscale yet welcoming. It’s one of those rare places where the lighting actually does you favors!

​The Food & Drink
​The menu is diverse, offering a great mix of global cuisines. The presentation is top-tier—everything from the cocktails to the dim sum arrives looking like a work of art.

​A Note on the Palate
​The food is undeniably high-quality, though it’s worth noting that the kitchen leans toward a bolder, spicier flavor profile.

​The Pro: The spices are fresh and aromatic, giving the dishes a real "zing" that stands out.
​The Caution: If you have a lower spice tolerance, you might find some dishes a bit intense.

​Tip: Don't hesitate to ask the servers to dial back the heat when you order; they are quite accommodating! Pairing your meal with one of their signature mocktails or shakes also helps balance out the fire.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Blabber All Day recently and had a great experience overall! One of the major plus points is their valet parking facility, which makes things so much easier in a busy area like this.

We had a reservation via Zomato, and thankfully we did—because the place was fully packed! Booking in advance really helped us avoid the wait.

Once seated, the service was very attentive. A modern touch I appreciated was that there’s no physical menu—each table has a QR code you can scan to order directly, including for cocktails, appetizers, and mains. Another thoughtful feature is the “ring for service” button on each table, which alerts the staff directly instead of having to call them over repeatedly—very convenient!

The ambience is chic and aesthetic, with dim lighting and a peaceful vibe, perfect for a relaxed evening.

Here’s what we ordered:
•	Cheesy Stuffed Mushrooms – Juicy with mild, flavorful stuffing. A good start.
•	Crackling Rolls (Sushi) – Absolutely mind-blowing! So good that we reordered.
•	Edamame Truffle Dim Sum – Wasn’t a fan of this one. It looked good but lacked the punch.
•	Berry Smoke Cocktail – Great presentation and a refreshing mix of berries and herbs.
•	Spaghetti Aglio Olio with Pepperoni – Taste was decent, but it was on the drier side.

The staff was friendly and efficient, making the entire experience smooth and enjoyable. I’d definitely recommend this place for a date night, an evening out with friends, family get-togethers, or even colleague dinners.

Tip: Make a reservation in advance to avoid waiting, and if you’re booking via Zomato, you can also avail 20% off when you pay through the app.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Tonight we dined at this cute little place that specialises in Baos and Sliders. The interiors were really cute as well as premium looking - though it was a small place, they had kept it really well maintained and was rather adorable.

Service is really quick. Everything is assembled quickly and served hot in front of you. Since it’s barely been two months since they’ve started, the owner is also really actively involved helping diners by recommending dishes and explaining the concept of the place to people.

Concept wise I like how they’ve kept the menu really simple - they want to focus on Baos and sliders and do that well - not lose focus on what’s important- the soft, bounciness of the Baos and the incredible fillings.

They make sure they make every single item that’s served on the table in house. Right from the sauces to the Bao to the breads - every single thing is made with TLC.

I love the fact that they allow half portions of food which lets you pair and taste more variety of food. Here’s what we tried:

1. Buttermilk chicken Bao - this is the quintessential combination that you really can’t go wrong with and they do it so very well.

2. Freedom Fries - these were you’re typical home fries made with lots of cheese sauce and veggies.

3. Lamb Seekh Bao - loved the Indian touch to this, the Bao was stuffed with Seekh and oodles of mint chutney

4. The coconut crusted prawns Bao - another favourite, it had crunchy, battered prawns with a spicy schezwan sauce.

5. Fish and chips slider - loved this one, it was the bhetki fish along with thinly sliced chips in a slider. Just perfect squish and crunch.

6. Chettinad Prawns Bao - The prawns were basted in a spicy, South Indian style sauce.

7. Miso Fish Slider - Fish in a miso sauce with sesame buns.

8. Gluten Free Mini Donuts - these were another favourite. They were gluten free and yet so so moist, soft and delicious.

9. Snickers - this was creamy, rich, heavenly and full of chocolate and peanut butter. I’d come back for this.

Loved the concept of the place with their unusual sliders and Baos. The price points were fair for a two piece good quality food dish being served. Loved it

Dynasty: The Indo-Chinese Restaurant That Doesn’t Need Buzz
Five stars aren’t enough, but they’ll have to do.
Dynasty operates in that rare territory where quality speaks louder than Instagram followers. This unpretentious neighborhood spot has mastered the art of authentic Indo-Chinese cooking — the kind that requires skill, not shortcuts.
Order the Chicken Lollipop and you’ll understand immediately. Each piece is a study in balance: crisp exterior, succulent interior, perfectly seasoned. The Manchow Soup arrives with the kind of umami depth that makes you wonder why other restaurants even bother. The Crispy Spinach Chicken demands respect, while the Crispy Thread Chicken delivers texture with purpose. These aren’t interpretations — they’re the genuine article.
But the real revelation lies in the Sour Chili and Sichuan dips. Layered, bold, and unapologetically complex, they’re the kind of accompaniments that transform a meal into an experience. The lemon iced tea cuts through it all with perfect timing.
What distinguishes Dynasty, though, is the service. The team moves with purpose, never intrusive, always present. It’s a family restaurant in the truest sense — one that makes you feel like you belong.
In a city saturated with forgettable Indo-Chinese, Dynasty reminds you why authenticity never goes out of style.

Dynasty Restaurant, Khar West: A Chinese Culinary Journey

Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West, Mumbai, is a haven for Chinese food enthusiasts. This popular eatery has been delighting taste buds with its authentic and flavorful dishes for years. Whether you're craving spicy, tangy, or sweet, Dynasty has something to offer.

One of the must-try dishes at Dynasty is their Crispy Spinach Paneer. This vegetarian delight features tender cubes of paneer coated in a crispy batter and tossed with fresh spinach. The combination of textures and flavors is simply irresistible. For a refreshing drink to complement your meal, try their Ice Lemon Tea. The tartness of the lemon combined with the sweetness of the tea makes it a perfect thirst quencher.

If you're looking for something spicy, the Paneer Chilli is a great option. Tender pieces of paneer are stir-fried with a spicy chili sauce, making it a fiery dish that will leave your taste buds tingling. For a unique twist on Chinese cuisine, try the Schezwan Crispy Veg. This dish features mixed vegetables coated in a crispy batter and tossed in a spicy Schezwan sauce.

For a satisfying main course, consider the Veg Burnt Garlic Rice or the Veg Malaysian Noodles. Both dishes are packed with flavor and are sure to leave you feeling full and satisfied. Dynasty also offers a variety of Indian Chinese dishes, combining traditional Indian flavors with Chinese cooking techniques.

To start your meal, the Manchow Soup is a classic choice. This flavorful soup is packed with vegetables and a hint of spice. For a refreshing and tangy drink, try the Sweet and Salty Lime Soda. The combination of sweet and salty flavors is a unique and refreshing treat.

Whether you're a seasoned Chinese food lover or new to the cuisine, Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West is a must-visit. With its delicious food, friendly service, and inviting atmosphere, it's no wonder why this restaurant is so popular among locals and tourists alike.

Pretty average experience. The authenticity of the food is good & so is the ambience. But the staff really needs training. The service was underwhelming. There's no clarity as to which language the staff is comfortable in, they are clueless if the dishes are available or not. I guess, the staff went 5-6 times to just confirm if the appetizers we were asking for is available or not. It's understandable if a few ingredients are not available on a given day, but if from 8 dishes, only 2 are available then the menu needs some reconsideration. 4 chicken wings for Rs. 499 which were nothing special.

Only the spring roll & momos were superb.

They add 10% service charges, which is removed it requested. They also had Bihu special pitha/sweets available. The quality was good but the price is too high. Rs. 300 for laru & Rs. 330 for Til pitha is too high.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my second visit to Singju, and it was absolutely amazing! We tried their traditional Singju, which instantly brought back memories of home. The Bhoot Jolokia Chicken Momos were perfectly delicious, packed with spice, veggies, and chicken. The Umarok Chicken Wings were another highlight—spicy, flavorful, and so satisfying. Paired with a refreshing lime juice, the whole meal was just perfect. If you’re looking for a homely and authentic North East India food experience, Singju is definitely the place to be!

P.S. As someone from Manipur, I can proudly say this is the real taste of home 🤩

featured_reviews.name: Nikita
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were excited to try some authentic North-Eastern food and were pleasantly surprised by how good it tasted. The menu offered a nice range of vegetarian options, which was impressive since most North-Eastern meals tend to include fish or meat. We ordered the Manipuri and Nepali thalis. Both were flavorful, well-prepared, and gave a genuine taste of the region.

Unfortunately, the experience was let down by the service. Our food took almost an hour to arrive, and despite asking multiple times, each server assured us it would be ready in “10 minutes”, which wasn’t true. No one came by to apologise for the delay, and it felt like the staff just didn’t care.

Even though the food itself was excellent, the poor service overshadowed everything. Sadly, we wouldn’t return, which is a pity given how delicious the dishes were.

featured_reviews.name: Abhinay Junghare
featured_reviews.review_text: The experience was highly satisfactory, particularly the Assamese cuisine. It is certainly worth recommending.

featured_reviews.name: Yi Ping Bong
featured_reviews.review_text: What an utterly underrated place serving a myriad of northeastern flavours! Our group had a fun time sampling the different thalis from Assam, Nepal, Manipur and Naga. I ordered the smoked pork manipuri thali, which awakened my senses (and sinus) with each tiny bowl bursting with flavors that surprises with each taste. Food took awhile to reach us since we placed 6 thali orders in one shot but boy was it worth it. Even the fried chicken appetizer was delicious with its umami bomb of a batter.

featured_reviews.name: J S
featured_reviews.review_text:
For a person very new to north eastern cuisine this was one of the most interesting restaurants I have been to. It is a tiny place with a few but comfortable tables and a good overall ambience.

Highly excited about the food we dove right into ordering the appetizers and soup.

First one to come was their prawns thupka soup - which was perfection. Flavourful broth, nice firm noodles just what was needed.

Next was pork momos which was served with a small pork soup. The momos had nicely flavoured meat in adequate quantity and with the soup were just so flavourful.

The next two dishes to come were the pork ribs and chicken wings from their specials part of the menu. The first two bites revealed a ton of smoky flavours but then the spice kicked in, which we eventually discovered was from bhoot jhalokia peppers. We powered through them teary eyed, loved the experience but can't say will try it again. But if spicy food is your domain, I would say you must try it.

The mains were a curry with fermented bamboo and pork and plain rice and also a portion of pork fried rice. We absolutely loved the pork fried rice. The curry had a flavour which was new and unique to us and some of us liked it while others did not.

The dessert was a red / purple rice kheer.. but it was really disappointing.

The service is friendly and acceptable.

Will go back to try more things on their menu without the bhoot jhalokia.😀

featured_reviews.name: saumya poddar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goh jia Ting - restaurant in bandra, had been on our list for a while, so after a show, we decided to finally give it a try. To be honest, walking into an almost empty restaurant was a little concerning. We were only the second occupied table, and the place remained virtually vacant throughout our visit. Still, we were extremely hungry and the overwhelmingly positive reviews online convinced us to stay and order.

Unfortunately, things went downhill from there.

One of the strangest parts of the evening was the service. At one point, a staff member stood directly in front of our table, watching us eat for an uncomfortably long time. It wasn’t attentive service—it felt intrusive and awkward. She only moved after we specifically requested her to. It genuinely made us uncomfortable, as though we were being monitored rather than hosted.

When I requested disposable chopsticks, the staff said they had them but then handed me what looked like a stranded stirrers and then later confessed that they don’t have disposable chopstick, then why say yes at the first place. Super careless and unprofessional.

The food was even worse. The prawn tempura roll tasted like it had been fried in old, stale oil. Instead of gyoza, we were served something that resembled chicken momos. The lobster roll was completely inedible and was left untouched after a few bites.

The cocktail we ordered, made with star fruit, was equally disappointing. It was so bad that we replaced it with a simple whisky just to avoid any more unpleasant surprises.

After struggling through the starters, we decided not to risk ordering anything else and left for another restaurant to have dinner. The entire experience felt like a complete waste of money.

What started as a restaurant we were genuinely excited to try ended up being one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve had in Bandra. Between the awkward service, poor food quality, disappointing drinks, and overall lacklustre experience, we left wondering how the glowing reviews online could possibly reflect what we experienced.

There are far too many great dining options in Bandra to spend your time and money here.

PLEASE DO NOT VISIT, would not recommend at all.

We had a 10:00 PM reservation and were only seated at 11:00 PM after standing inside the restaurant for an hour in complete chaos. What’s the point of making a booking? There was absolutely no system to manage reservations or waiting guests — no clarity on who came first, no communication, just a crowded, irritated room full of people arguing. Once seated, it didn’t get better. No water or napkins were served until halfway through our meal. We had to ask multiple times for something as basic as a spoon — which still never came. Service felt careless and disorganized throughout.

We ordered black bean veggies but were served some butter garlic gravy that tasted purely of cornstarch — no salt, no flavor, completely inedible. By 11:30 PM we were so hungry and frustrated that we didn’t even bother asking for it to be changed, but it was honestly one of the worst dishes we’ve had.

To top it off, we had to ask for the bill three times, and even then it took 20 minutes. Zero regard for guests’ time.

Completely ruined our evening. When you’re paying premium prices at a so-called upscale restaurant, basic service, organization, and edible food should not be too much to expect. Would not recommend.

The noodles were super flavorful, perfectly spicy, and tasted absolutely delicious. Every bite was full of flavor, and the portion size was also great. If you love spicy food, this dish is definitely a must-try!

featured_reviews.name: Anshul Parkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place after a college dance party with my friends. We were extremely tired and just wanted a good meal near Bandra station, so we decided to try Hakka Mama since it was nearby.

Unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing. 😞

The service was extremely slow — we literally had to call the waiter again and again just to place our order. It honestly felt like they were doing us a favor by serving food. While waiting, we also noticed multiple rats running around inside the restaurant, which was very unhygienic and uncomfortable. 🐀

Since we were exhausted, we still decided to stay, hoping the food would arrive soon. But the wait time was unbelievable. We entered at around 8:30 PM and didn't get our food until much later. We ended up leaving at around 12 AM — nearly 3.5 hours spent for a simple dinner. ⏰

Overall:
• Very poor service
• Extremely long waiting time
• Hygiene issues (rats inside restaurant)
• Huge waste of time

Would not recommend, especially if you're hungry or short on time. Very disappointing experience. 👎

featured_reviews.name: iram khan
featured_reviews.review_text: Amazing cozy spot right nice to the bustling bandra station. The food is amazing so is the service. Huge thanks to Shahid and Muntasir for their great suggestions and service. Please try the Bao buns they make it fresh!

featured_reviews.name: Prithu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Royal China is the kind of place that makes you feel underdressed even when you are dressed well.

The ambience is classy without trying too hard, dim lighting, elegant interiors, and the sort of atmosphere where people suddenly start speaking 20 percent softer. It has that proper fine dining energy where even the water arrives looking expensive.

The food absolutely holds up to the reputation. The menu is extensive, packed with authentic Chinese dishes that actually taste refined instead of just aggressively spicy. The dim sums are a standout, and the overall quality of ingredients is noticeable from the first bite itself.

Service is polished and attentive without hovering over your table every two minutes asking if “everything is okay.” They know what they are doing, which makes the whole experience feel smooth.

Yes, it is expensive. The bill arrives with enough confidence to remind you this is not your local takeaway spot. But unlike many overpriced fine dining places, this one at least gives you the feeling that your money went somewhere meaningful.

Final verdict: Elegant, reliable, and consistently good. Come for the food, stay for the feeling of temporarily having your life together.

featured_reviews.name: Sweet Sour
featured_reviews.review_text:
For lovers of authentic Chinese cuisine, Royal China offers a refined and memorable dining experience, combining elegant ambiance with thoughtfully curated flavors.

I began with their mocktails — the Jade Green Cooler and Pearl of the Orient. Both were beautifully presented and refreshingly balanced, with subtle yet distinct flavor profiles that made them perfect palate openers.

The starters truly set the tone for the meal. The Spicy Lotus Root stood out with its crisp texture and bold seasoning, delivering a satisfying crunch in every bite. The Crispy Silken Tofu with Sweet Chilli Sauce was equally impressive — delicately crisp on the outside while remaining soft and silky within, complemented by a flavorful sweet and mildly spicy glaze.

Moving on to the main course, the Burnt Chilli Garlic Noodles were rich, aromatic, and packed with deep, smoky flavors that lingered pleasantly. Paired with this were the Steamed Wontons in Spicy Sauce, which were light yet indulgent, coated in a well-balanced sauce that added just the right amount of heat without overpowering the dish.

The experience concluded on a decadent note with the Chocolate Dome dessert — a visually stunning and indulgent creation that perfectly balanced richness and sweetness, making it a delightful end to the meal.

Overall, Royal China stands out as a sophisticated destination for those seeking high-quality Chinese cuisine, where each dish is crafted with attention to detail and flavor harmony.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Royal China which is 10 mnts ride from Bandra station. We had a really nice premium dining experience. The ambience is so soothing, dim lights and soft music.
We tried the Prawns Cheung Fung, Egg Fried Rice, Prawns in Hot Garlic Sauce, and Sizzling Brownie everything was fresh, flavorful, and well prepared. Ended our meal with a sizzling brownie which was amazing. The brownie was so gooey, filled with walnuts.
The entire team provided great hospitality. Special thanks to Leiya - very polite and attentive, and  manager Arjun was extremely welcoming, making our dining experience worth remembering.
Overall, a great experience.

featured_reviews.name: tanishka_on_the_go
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a lovely dinner at Royal China.
The ambience is calm, classy and very comfortable.
We loved the Coconut Pearl and Pearl of the Orient drinks.
Spicy prawn wontons were my favourite starter.
Satay chicken and truffle tenderloin were full of flavour.
Chicken Hakka noodles were perfectly cooked and comforting.
The crème brûlée was a perfect way to end the meal.
Great food quality and presentation.
Definitely a nice place for a relaxed dinner or date night.

featured_reviews.name: Porus V
featured_reviews.review_text: Royal China has been around long enough to become one of those restaurants that people in the city trust when it comes to Asian food. And that trust is well earned! The food is consistently really good. Love the dim sums, Crispy prawn Cheung Fun and the wonton soup here. Nothing feels perfunctory. Also the crispy aromatic duck is a regular highlight for many, and so is the crab fried rice. The space is elegant, unpretentious, and consistently good and reliable every time.

featured_reviews.name: Tanishka Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Royal China and the experience was amazing. The place has a very classy and elegant vibe. The staff was extremely polite and welcoming, which made the visit even better.
We started with Orange Blossom, a refreshing mocktail full of fruity flavours of orange, cranberry, and apple. The Yuzu Viking was another favourite with pineapple juice and elderflower syrup, very light and fresh.
For starters, the Belgian Pork Dumplings were soft, flavourful, and perfectly steamed. The Smoked Shredded Chicken was crispy, garlicky, and had a nice crunch from the vegetables.
The highlight for me was the Truffle Tenderloin, seared to perfection and served on a sizzling plate with that rich truffle aroma. The Hong Kong Street Style Noodles were simple yet very tasty, with beansprouts and spring onion adding the right crunch.
We ended with the Chocolate Dome, which was a delightful surprise with mud cake and ice cream inside. Overall, Royal China is definitely a place I would recommend for anyone who enjoys great food, a classy setting, and excellent service.

featured_reviews.name: yasmeen sayad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited House of Mandarin, Bandra for lunch and had a pleasant experience overall, mainly because of the lovely seating arrangement and the extremely courteous staff. The ambiance truly sets the right tone.

However, the food didn’t match the expectations we had from the place.

What we tried:

Crispy Lamb Mandarin Style:
The flavours were nice and it did have a good crisp, but it turned out quite oily and a bit salty. Additionally, the lamb itself was hard to distinguish while chewing.

Crispy Prawn Cheung Fun:
This was the highlight of our meal. The prawns were extremely fresh, and the dish had a perfectly balanced taste. Definitely recommended.

Mandarin Fried Rice in Lotus Leaf (Chicken):
Expected this to be a standout, but it was fairly average and didn’t have the depth of flavour we anticipated.

Chicken Manchurian Gravy:
Unfortunately, this was too salty, making it difficult to pair with the fried rice.

Overall, it’s still a decent spot for lunch thanks to the ambience and service, but the dishes could use some refinement to match the vibe and expectations.

featured_reviews.name: Jyothis Thaliath
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my second visit to House of Mandarin in Bandra, and I must say it has improved a lot since my last time. It is slightly on the expensive side compared to other Chinese restaurants, but the food quality and flavors make it worth it. The place is well suited for families for both lunch and dinner.

We started with fried corn and water chestnut starter, which turned out to be a hidden gem, perfectly crispy and full of flavor. The prawns tempura had a lighter coating this time, though I wish it had been a bit crunchier like before.

The yummy spicy crab soup lived up to its name. It was enough for two people to have plenty.

The blue pea flower fried rice with smoked chicken was the star of the meal, beautifully smoky and absolutely delicious. I wish we could have one more serving of it.

Coming to main course, glazed pork had a different flavor than I expected; I was looking for a honey-glazed sweetness, but that was my bad.

We ended the ordeal with the ice cream brownie sizzler, which was outstanding with its rich caramel sauce and perfect balance of textures.

Overall, a wonderful dining experience with delicious food and noticeable improvement since my previous visit. House of Mandarin continues to be one of the better Chinese options in Bandra.
